profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the BONSEYES pipeline integration workstream and the embedded deployment workstream ahead of a consortium dry-run demo. The team is preparing a shared handoff package for two showcase applications—keyword spotting and image classification—so that a partner site can reproduce the end-to-end flow from model artifact to on-device execution through the IoT hub. The agenda is to align on what artifacts will be uploaded to the shared workspace, which pipeline build and model artifacts the deployment team will use, and what status can be reported as 'validated' in the review sheet. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear agreement on Thursday's handoff: which files each person will provide, what will be linked in the consortium folder, and what status update will be sent to the broader project team.

members.name: Elena Varga
members.expertise: ML workflow orchestration, dataset-to-training pipelines, model packaging, consortium integration
members.background: Elena coordinates the BONSEYES end-to-end pipeline across data ingestion, training, and partner-facing deliverables, and previously worked on reproducible ML workflows for research consortia where standardized artifacts and registry releases were emphasized.
members.private_state: She wants the dry-run package to look clean and stable for external partners, avoid last-minute surprises from lab-specific dependencies, and keep the deliverables aligned with the officially published pipeline release rather than internal experimental setups.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'reference model,' they mean the frozen ONNX artifact exported by the training stage before any deployment-specific graph rewrites.
The '2.3 build' refers to the signed container image already published in the consortium registry, because only registry-published builds count as the shared pipeline version.
A model is 'validated on device' once it has completed at least one successful end-to-end run on the target board through the expected pipeline path, including IoT hub handoff if applicable.
A partner handoff 'deployment bundle' should contain only the model package, example inputs/outputs, and brief instructions, because runtimes and board toolchains are maintained separately.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.expertise: Edge inference optimization, LPDNN integration, cross-compilation, board-level benchmarking
members.background: Ravi maintains the deployment side of the BONSEYES stack, integrating trained models into LPDNN, tuning them for embedded targets, and validating runtime behavior on development boards used in the project lab.
members.private_state: He wants to preserve the exact lab setup that produced reliable embedded results, avoid being blamed for partner reproducibility issues caused by missing dependencies, and keep using the lab-proven build that already contains deployment fixes not yet reflected in the public registry image.
hidden_assumptions: The 'reference model' is the imported and normalized graph inside the LPDNN toolchain, because that is the actual artifact from which device executables are produced.
The '2.3 build' means the lab-mirrored 2.3-rc2 container that everyone on the deployment side has been using, even if the public registry image with the same release label differs slightly.
A system is only 'validated on device' when repeated on-board runs have confirmed stable latency and memory behavior under the deployment configuration, not just a single successful inference.

A proper 'deployment bundle' must be self-contained, including runtime libraries, board-specific scripts, and calibration/cache artifacts, so a partner can reproduce the tested setup without guessing missing pieces.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants refer to attaching or using the 'reference model' for the handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the trainer-exported ONNX model that serves as the canonical artifact for the pipeline.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the LPDNN-imported and graph-normalized model that serves as the canonical artifact for deployment.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this project, both training and deployment teams routinely use 'reference model' to mean the artifact they personally treat as authoritative, and because both artifacts are closely related versions of the same network, surface agreement sounds perfectly natural.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants say they will use or upload the '2.3 build' or 'latest 2.3 container.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the officially published 2.3 container in the consortium registry.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the lab-mirrored 2.3-rc2 image that already includes a deployment-side importer patch.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The version label is almost identical and both consider their artifact the obvious current build, so neither expects that '2.3' could refer to two nearby but non-identical containers.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants discuss whether the applications are 'validated on device' for the review sheet.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a successful end-to-end execution on the target board that demonstrates the pipeline path works.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means benchmark-grade confirmation with repeated runs and stable resource measurements on the target board.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'validated' often functions as a lightweight status word rather than a carefully defined acceptance criterion, so both hear the same positive status signal and assume their own threshold is shared.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants talk about preparing the 'deployment bundle' for the partner site.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the bundle includes only handoff-facing artifacts: model package, sample input/output, and a short README.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the bundle includes everything needed to reproduce the deployment environment: runtime libraries, board scripts, and calibration/cache files in addition to the model.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see themselves as discussing the same deliverable and neither wants to derail a coordination call by itemizing contents that feel operationally obvious within their own workstream.
